_readme: Veggie Dex card data. One entry per vegetable. status = 'grown' or 'wishlist'. Months are 1-12. Unknown values must be the string 'Unknown'. latin/family carry a [n] citation like other facts. photo_focus = [x, y] crop centre as 0-1 fractions; photo_zoom >= 1 zooms in. Card order/ids come from reshuffle.py (family, then species, grown before wishlist); new cards get max id + 1 until the next reshuffle.

cards.name: Beetroot
cards.planting_window: Feb-Jul. Outdoors from late Mar/Apr once soil is 7°C+; Feb sowings need a bolt-resistant variety under fleece or cloches [1]
cards.harvest_window: Jun-Oct, at golf-ball to cricket-ball size; bigger roots can turn woody [1]
special_instructions: Soak seed in warm water for an hour before sowing [1]
Water every 10-14 days in dry spells; uneven watering splits roots, as seen on one of these [1]
Twist off leaves, keeping 4-5 on; store roots in dry sand or compost in a cool shed [1]

cards.name: Spring Onion
cards.planting_window: Sow from Mar, little and often every couple of weeks; hardy types late summer/early autumn for spring picking [1]
cards.harvest_window: Spring to autumn, about two months after sowing; overwintered hardy types from Mar [1]
special_instructions: Thin to about 2.5cm apart: crowding encourages downy mildew [1]
Water until established, then only in long dry spells (pots more often) [1]
Guard seedlings from slugs; watch for onion fly. Cloche hardy sowings in harsh winters [1]
recipes: Seared mackerel with chilli, cucumber & spring onion [3]

cards.name: Horseradish
cards.planting_window: Plant roots (thongs) or young plants in spring or early summer, upright with the top 5cm below the soil [1]
cards.harvest_window: Best in autumn or early winter after a frost; spring/summer lifting is possible with extra water. Young plants lightly from their 2nd autumn [1]
special_instructions: Spreads by roots and regrows from any piece left behind; a 30cm+ pot keeps it contained [1]
Lift up to half the roots each year and replant the rest [1]
Store whole roots in damp sand somewhere cool and dark; grate just before use [1]

cards.name: Turnip
cards.planting_window: Mar-mid Aug, little and often. Early types Mar-Jun (Feb under cloches); maincrop Jul-mid Aug [1]
cards.harvest_window: Early types May-Sep; maincrop from Oct onward. Leaves can be picked from spring [1]
special_instructions: Pick at golf-ball size for raw, tennis-ball for cooking; larger goes woody and bitter [1]
Water in dry spells or roots stay small, split or bolt [1]
Net against birds; watch for flea beetle and club root [1]

cards.name: Radish
cards.planting_window: Salad types Feb-Aug (Feb under cloches), small batches every few weeks [1]
cards.harvest_window: Late spring through summer, about 4-6 weeks after germination [1]
special_instructions: Keep evenly moist; uneven watering splits roots (split ones are still edible) [1]
Pull at about 2.5cm across before they turn woody or hot [1]
Flea beetle holes in leaves are usually just cosmetic [1]
recipes: Smacked radishes with sesame, sumac & mint [3]

cards.name: Cucumber
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors mid Feb-Apr (late Apr for outdoor crops), or direct late May/early Jun; plant out from early Jun once reliably above 12°C [1]
cards.harvest_window: Mid-summer to mid-autumn; pick small types at 15cm, full-sized at 20-25cm [1]
special_instructions: Water at the base in the morning, more as fruits form; keep leaves dry [1]
Train up supports; outdoors pinch out the tip after seven leaves [1]
Remove male flowers on all-female greenhouse types (bitter fruit); keep them on outdoor types [1]

cards.name: Giant Pumpkin
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors mid-late Apr at 18-21°C, or outdoors late May/early Jun after frost; trailing types 1.5m apart [2]
cards.harvest_window: Autumn, leaving fruit on the plant as long as possible but in before the first frost; cut with 10cm+ of stem [2]
special_instructions: For a giant, let just one fruit develop per plant and remove any others [2]
Water generously; high-potash feed every 10-14 days once the fruit swells; rest it on a tile off damp soil [2]
Pin runners down at the leaf joints so they root and take up more water [3]

cards.name: Courgette
cards.planting_window: Indoors Apr-early May at 18-21°C; outdoors late May/early Jun. Plant out in early summer, 90cm apart [1]
cards.harvest_window: Through summer, picked at 10-12.5cm long [1]
special_instructions: Keep soil moist; water the base, not the leaves, to limit powdery mildew [1]
In pots, high-potash feed every 10-14 days once fruits swell [1]
Frost-tender; cool spells can cause poor pollination and fruit rot [1]

cards.name: Chilli Pepper
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors Feb-Apr at about 21°C; plant out late May/early Jun once nights stay above 12°C, or grow on under cover [1]
cards.harvest_window: Mid-summer into autumn under glass; outdoor plants should start fruiting by Aug [1]
special_instructions: Keep compost evenly moist: dry plants drop their flower buds [1]
Weekly high-potash feed once flowering; pick some green to keep more chillies coming [1]
To overwinter, cut back and keep somewhere warm and bright, watering sparingly [1]

cards.name: Cherry Tomato
cards.planting_window: Sow late Feb-mid Mar for greenhouse, late Mar-early Apr for outdoors (18°C); plant out once reliably above 16°C [1]
cards.harvest_window: From mid-summer into autumn; pick fully coloured with the stalk on [1]
special_instructions: Cordons: pinch out side-shoots and stop after ~4 trusses outdoors; bush types keep theirs [1]
Water evenly to avoid splitting and blossom end rot; high-potash feed every 10-14 days [1]
Outdoor plants are blight-prone; don't grow in the same bed two years running [1]

cards.name: Aubergine
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors from Feb (Jan only if heated); plant out late May/early Jun after frost, or Apr-May under glass [1]
cards.harvest_window: From Aug, when full-sized, well coloured and glossy; protect outdoor plants by late Sep [1]
special_instructions: Needs 21°C+ to germinate; keep seedlings at 16-18°C [1]
Pinch out the tip at about 30cm; stake the main stem [1]
High-potash feed fortnightly once flowering; dull skin = over-ripe and bitter [1]

cards.name: Pea
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors Feb–Mar, or outdoors Mar–Jun once the soil reaches 10°C; plant out at about 20cm tall [1]
cards.harvest_window: Jun–Oct; pick regularly or plants stop flowering. Mangetout and sugarsnap at about 7.5cm long [1]
special_instructions: Support tall types with netting or canes, short types with twiggy pea sticks [1]
Mice eat new sowings, so start indoors; net against pigeons [1]
Water well at flowering and again two weeks later to swell pods [1]
recipes: Amritsari cod with green pea chutney [3]
Wild sea bass with pea and mint soup [3]
Chilled watercress soup with garden peas [3]

cards.name: Carrot
cards.planting_window: Main sowings Apr–early Jul; early types Feb–Mar under cloches or fleece. Sow small batches every 3–4 weeks [1]
cards.harvest_window: About 12–16 weeks after sowing, through summer into autumn; maincrops can stay in the ground into winter [1]
special_instructions: Cover with insect-proof mesh against carrot fly; sowing after mid-May avoids the first generation [1]
Thin to 5–7.5cm apart; stones and overcrowding cause forked roots [1]
Rarely needs watering, but uneven moisture splits roots; soak fortnightly in long dry spells [1]
recipes: Honey-roast carrots with orange and pistachios [3]
Glazed carrots with tarragon and garlic [3]

cards.name: Butternut Squash
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors mid–late Apr at 18–21°C, or outdoors late May–early Jun after the last frost [1]
cards.harvest_window: Autumn, before the first frost; cut with 10cm of stem, cure in the sun 7–10 days, store 3–6 months [1]
special_instructions: Trailing types need about 1.5m between plants, bush types 90cm [1]
Keep well watered, especially when fruiting; dry roots invite powdery mildew [1]
Raise fruit off damp soil on a tile or brick so it ripens in full sun [1]

cards.name: Red Kuri Squash
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors mid–late Apr at 18–21°C, or outdoors late May–early Jun after the last frost [1]
cards.harvest_window: Autumn, before the first frost; cut with 10cm of stem, cure in the sun 7–10 days, store 3–6 months [1]
special_instructions: Onion-type squash: 2–3 orange-red teardrop fruits per plant, 1.5–3kg each [2]
Trailing types need about 1.5m between plants; keep well watered when fruiting [1]
Cure in the sun 7–10 days, then store at 10–15°C with fruits not touching [1]

cards.name: Harlequin Squash
cards.planting_window: Sow indoors mid–late Apr at 18–21°C, or outdoors late May–early Jun after the last frost [1]
cards.harvest_window: Autumn, before the first frost; cut with 10cm of stem, cure in the sun 7–10 days, store 3–6 months [1]
special_instructions: Compact, bushy and early-maturing; holds the RHS Award of Garden Merit [2]
Striped acorn-shaped fruits up to about 700g may need support to keep them off the ground [2]
Bush types need about 90cm between plants; keep well watered when fruiting [1]
recipes: Pumpkin tarts with spinach and gorgonzola [4]

cards.name: Onion
cards.planting_window: Sets early–mid spring, or overwintering sets in autumn; seed mid-winter to mid-spring. Sets 10–15cm apart [1]
cards.harvest_window: Jul–Oct from spring sets and seed; Jun–Jul from autumn sets. Lift when the foliage yellows and topples [1]
special_instructions: Net or fleece new sets against birds until they root [1]
Water in dry spells while roots form; stop once bulbs swell in mid-summer [1]
Dry for about 2 weeks until papery, then store somewhere cool, light and airy [1]

cards.name: Garlic
cards.planting_window: Plant cloves mid-autumn to early winter (some types late winter–early spring), 15cm apart, tips 2.5cm deep [1]
cards.harvest_window: Autumn-planted: late spring to early summer; spring-planted: mid-summer to early autumn. Lift when leaves yellow [1]
special_instructions: Most types need 1–2 months at 0–10°C to form good bulbs [1]
Water in spring dry spells; stop once bulbs are well formed to avoid rot [1]
Watch for leek rust and white rot; dry 2–4 weeks before storing [1]
recipes: Grilled mussels with garlic and parsley [3]

cards.name: Potato
cards.planting_window: First earlies late Mar, second earlies early–mid Apr, maincrops mid-Apr to early May; 15cm deep [1]
cards.harvest_window: First earlies Jun–Jul, second earlies Jul–Aug, maincrops late Aug–Oct. Test a tuber before lifting [1]
special_instructions: Chit earlies from late Jan for 4–6 weeks; maincrops gain little [1]
Earth up from 23cm tall, leaving 10cm showing, to guard against frost and green tubers [1]
Water in dry weather; watch for blight, slugs and scab, and rotate each year [1]
recipes: Roast Jersey Royals with glazed pear and Roquefort [3]

cards.name: Parsnip
cards.planting_window: Sow outdoors Mar–early May once soil is about 12°C, 1cm deep; thin to 15cm apart [1]
cards.harvest_window: Lift when leaves die down in autumn, ideally after the first hard frost sweetens the roots; can stay in into winter [1]
special_instructions: Use fresh seed each year; seedlings can take 14–30 days to appear [1]
Deep, stone-free soil with no fresh manure, or roots fork [1]
Mesh against carrot fly; grow canker-resistant varieties such as 'Albion' [1]
recipes: Turmeric and curry leaf roast parsnips [3]
Maple-roasted parsnips with red wine vinegar [3]
Roast parsnips with bacon, olives, sage and sprout leaves [3]

cards.name: Leek
cards.planting_window: Plant April to June in the UK [2]
cards.harvest_window: Harvest from August to March in the UK [2]
special_instructions: Choose a sunny spot with free-draining soil [2]
Dig in compost or well-rotted manure [2]
Earth up leeks for long white shanks [2]
